subject: geography
title: Economic Development Adventure: Strategies
welcome_lead: Aid, trade, microfinance, fair trade — which strategies actually help countries develop?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography development strategies — aid, trade, microfinance, fair trade, Nigeria.
final_note: You weighed up real-world development strategies including a Nigeria NEE case study.

concepts.def: Aid from one country directly to another
Aid via international body (UN, World Bank)
Producers get fair, stable price for goods
Small loans to people without access to banks

walkthroughs.body_html:
Bilateral: country to country, sometimes 'tied' (must spend on donor goods).

Multilateral: pooled via UN/World Bank — less political.

NGO: charity-funded, often small-scale and grassroots (WaterAid wells).

UK spends roughly 0.5% of GNI on overseas aid.

Trade can lift more people out of poverty than aid — but only on fair terms.

Fairtrade: bananas, coffee, cocoa farmers get a minimum price + premium for community projects.

Microfinance (Grameen Bank, Bangladesh): small loans (often to women) for goats, sewing machines — pay back into the community fund.

Nigeria is Africa's largest economy. Around 200+ million people.

Oil: 90% of export earnings — but vulnerable to price swings and pollution in the Niger Delta.

TNCs: Shell, Unilever provide jobs but profits can leave the country.

Manufacturing: textiles, Nollywood film industry are growing fast.

mcqs.q: Why is HDI a better measure of development than GNI per capita?
options: HDI combines income, life expectancy and education, capturing quality of life — GNI per capita is just average income and hides inequality and non-economic wellbeing.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Because HDI measures how happy people are.
The Brandt Line is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.

mcqs.q: Why is the Brandt Line considered outdated?
options: The Brandt Line is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The Brandt Line still accurately divides rich and poor countries today.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Drawn in 1980, it predates the rise of NICs (China, India, Brazil) and globalisation — countries like South Korea, Singapore and Chile no longer fit neatly on the 'poor south' side.
